messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager: Region-trending alert — Azure WestCentral. Multiple private-networked customers report intermittent DNS resolution failures to our private endpoints. Severity: P2. Auto-alert triggered at 2026-03-15T10:13:19Z

oncall-tim: ack. I’m on it, jumping in now.

neteng-anne: seeing similar noisy NXDOMAIN and slow responses from our vWAN edge in westcentral. Flow logs show spikes in UDP retries to our private DNS pair.

infra-ryan: I can access the VNet DNS from the control plane ok, but from some on-prem circuits the queries fail or time out. Looks like split-horizon behavior might be flipping between internal and public answers.

sre-ops: customers on DirectConnect-equivalent / ExpressRoute-style links are the most impacted — latency + 5xxs for initial handshakes hitting private endpoints. Possible asymmetric routing on the Azure peering?

oncall-tim: @neteng-anne can you dump the vWAN route table and BGP state? pastebin or gist the outputs. Also, any recent config changes to the private DNS zones?

neteng-anne: past 30m no config pushes from infra. Pasting key outputs: 
```
# vwan route-summary
active-paths: 3
peer-status: established
bgp-flaps: 0
private-dns-views: primary=ok, secondary=stale
```
and from the peering edge: 
```
udp-drop-counters: iface1: 42, iface2: 0
as-path: consistent
```
Link: https://internal-gists/abc123 (redacted)

se-customer-lynn: customers are reporting auth failures as well because our initial TLS handshake hits wrong IP when DNS gives public IP. We saw spikes starting 10:05Z. Impacting ~6 customers, two are in active production.

oncall-tim: rolling mitigation idea: temporarily override private DNS zone TTL->30s and force refresh, plus route prepend to prefer backup peering. @infra-ryan can you prepare the TTL change and a BGP prepend on the backup path?

infra-ryan: TTL change ready to apply. Will push to primary private-zone in 2m. BGP prepend on backup requires a change window but I can apply immediate community change to prefer backup. Doing it now.

neteng-anne: applying community to steer traffic to backup peering. Monitoring.

incident-bot: Action logged: TTL change applied by infra-ryan at 2026-03-15T10:20:03Z. Community prepend applied by neteng-anne at 2026-03-15T10:20:45Z.

sre-ops: quick check — synthetic probes to private endpoints show success rate improving from 74% -> 92% after community. Still seeing occasional HD-lookup failures.

oncall-tim: good. @se-customer-lynn start notifying impacted customers with the mitigation note and ETA for root cause investigation. Mark as under investigation, avoiding making any promises on SLA until RC found. Use runbook template: "intermittent-private-dns-flap".

se-customer-lynn: notified customers at 10:28Z. Sent: "We are aware of intermittent DNS resolution issues to private endpoints in Azure WestCentral. Short-term mitigation applied (routing adjustment + TTL refresh). We will follow up with a post-incident summary."

neteng-anne: investigating telemetry — control plane logs show split-horizon engine toggled view between private and public answers after a background sync with Azure Private DNS service. Suspect service-side race when zones synced across peering instances. Opening SR with Azure.

infra-ryan: capturing pcap from the edge for correlation and uploading to secure bucket. Link: https://internal-storage/pcaps/1729999999.pcap (internal-only).

sre-ops: start collecting customer logs and sample queries for correlation. Add to incident doc. Also bumping retention of debug logs for 24h so we don’t miss window.

oncall-tim: handing off to @neteng-anne for deeper RCA and Azure SR. I’ll stay on as backup for escalation. Please update this thread with SR number and progress. If escalation to Azure PG needed, tag me. Handoff at 10:36Z.

neteng-anne: ack and taking lead. SR opened with Azure at 10:40Z — SR# AZ-210-99827. Azure acknowledged potential private DNS view replication lag. They’re collecting internal traces.

se-customer-lynn: customer A reports intermittent auth failures resolved after 10:22Z. Customer B still reporting occasional 5xxs at 10:33Z, but less frequent.

sre-ops: monitoring: current success rate 97% from our probes, customer-facing errors down 85% compared to peak. Marking impact: partial degradation for specific on-prem circuits that experienced split-horizon flips.

incident-bot: severity updated to P3 at 2026-03-15T11:00:00Z due to mitigation reducing broader impact.

neteng-anne: will continue to work with Azure on fix (likely longer-term change to DNS view syncing). Will post update when SR provides root cause or patch.

oncall-tim: thanks everyone. After-action: collect timeline, config diffs, pcap, and customer impact table. Schedule brief postmortem with neteng/infra/sre in 48h.

se-customer-lynn: confirmed. Customers asked for postmortem. I’ll draft impact notices once RCA available.

incident-bot: Incident thread closed for active paging at 2026-03-15T11:10:00Z (no further escalation).

neteng-anne: Note for postmortem — consider adding a probe that validates private vs public DNS answers for critical zones across on-prem links to detect split-horizon flips earlier.

infra-ryan: Also suggest an automated route-failover policy for private peering that triggers community steer + TTL bump when query error thresholds exceeded.

oncall-tim: Agreed. Thanks team.
